title: the gate usage lines list the catalogue, not the active set
body:
# 0007: the gate usage lines list the catalogue, not the active set

## Tags

gatecmd, help, D4, D11, WP-11, needs-ruling

## Summary

`run_builtin_gate` (lib/gatecmd:47 and :56) prints its usage line from `builtin_options_for "$cmd"` -- the RAW CATALOGUE. In Baize (languages `[elixir, shell]`, `fmt md` disabled) that renders:

```
usage: baize fmt <elixir|rust|swift|md|all>
usage: baize check <compile|format|deps|clippy|toolchain|critic|all>
```

Three of the four fmt arms it advertises refuse with rc 2 when invoked (`'baize fmt rust' is not available here: this project does not declare the 'rust' language`), and `clippy` likewise. The refusals themselves are exact and correctly reasoned -- the dispatcher knows the active set -- but the usage line names things that do not resolve, which is D4's rule ("help is GENERATED from what actually resolves") violated in one corner. A reader in a mixed fleet cannot tell from the usage line which arms THIS project has.

## Why it is not just a string fix

The active set is computed dispatcher-side (D11 language activation + config `enabled:`), and `run_builtin_gate` runs in the gate command's process with only what the dispatcher exports (`DEVBIN_LANGUAGES`, `DEVBIN_FMT_ARMS` -- the latter fmt-specific). Filtering the catalogue inside gatecmd means either re-deriving activation there (a second copy of the D11 logic -- Highlander breach) or the dispatcher exporting the active option list per gate command (a new export, one more seam). That is a design call, so this is filed rather than patched mid-migration.

## Found by

The Baize migration's dispatch probes (WP-11, 2026-08-09) -- the eighth base defect found by building the next thing. The generated GLOBAL help gets this right (it lists exactly the active options); only the gate commands' own usage lines read the raw catalogue.

**Second sighting, same day, worse shape (Lamplight):** `usage: lamplight fmt <elixir|rust|swift|md|all>` -- all four advertised arms are DISABLED in this project, and the one arm that actually exists (`ldn`, config-declared) is ABSENT from the line. The usage string both advertises what refuses and omits what runs. Config-declared options never appear because `builtin_options_for` reads only the catalogue.

## Options

1. Dispatcher exports `DEVBIN_ACTIVE_<CMD>` (option names, space-joined) for each gate command; gatecmd prints that. One derivation, one new export.
2. gatecmd filters via `builtin_option_lang` x `DEVBIN_LANGUAGES` + a disabled-set export. Re-derives half of activation; drifts when activation grows a new axis (it already has three: language, opt-in, enabled).
3. Decline: the refusal messages are precise, the global help is right, and the usage line is a hint not a contract. Record the reason here.

## Resolution (2026-08-09, hv's pick: option 1)

One derivation, one export. `command_options` already IS the active set (config-declared actives in declared order, then active built-ins -- the list `all` fans over and the global help renders), so the dispatcher exports `DEVBIN_ACTIVE_{CHECK,DB,DOCS,FMT,TEST}` and gatecmd's `usage_options_for` prints the export, with the raw catalogue only as the outside-the-dispatcher fallback. No re-derivation lands in gatecmd, so the Highlander concern in option 2 never arises. Three tests, each seen red against the catalogue-printing code first: the Lamplight shape (declared `ldn` appears, disabled/undeclared arms vanish) and the Baize shape (`clippy` gone from an elixir-only project's check line).
